mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate directly lowers discount rates for equity valuation models, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependency.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 5.5% in a 3-month window signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.5% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad consumer demand contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days through reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative returns: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Manufacturing slowdown (INDPRO annualized growth < 0.5%) indicates industrial output contraction that reduces corporate profit margins, driving negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: In INDPRO YoY growth < 0.5% periods, S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strengthening labor market (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly) boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in less than 50% of PAYEMS growth > 0.5% instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 1-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY growth > 3.5%) triggers Federal Reserve tightening expectations, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY growth exceeds 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (GDPC1 annualized growth > 3.0%) signals robust consumer and business spending, boosting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: In GDPC1 annualized growth > 3.0% periods, S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in FEDFUNDS and elevated UNRATE indicate dual economic shocks (monetary tightening + labor market weakness) that depress equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint occurrence of rising FEDFUNDS and high UNRATE fails to predict negative returns: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.
